page: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dpsv6 family. It is powered by an ARM64-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading resource sharing. It is equipped with 256 GB of RAM, translating to 4 GB of memory per core. The processor features a 128 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates that the D64ps_v6 delivers top-tier multi-core performance. In multi-threaded workloads, the instance achieves top-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory performance is a notable strength, with uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths reaching top-tier classifications at 463.82 GB/sec and 203.11 GB/sec respectively. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the average tier.

Given its high core density and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D64ps_v6 is highly efficient for multi-threaded, parallelizable workloads. It demonstrates top-tier capability in static web serving throughput, software compilation using Clang, and database operations. It also shows strong performance in Redis SET operations. While it handles medium-sized LLM text generation adequately, it is less suited for single-threaded tasks or heavy local storage-dependent operations due to the lack of local NVMe drives. The ARM64 architecture offers a resource-dense, cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 instances for scale-out workloads, web serving, and database hosting.

This hardware profile makes the instance highly effective and cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads, including database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and scale-out enterprise applications.
